title: JavaScript Metaprogramming Applied Check
description: Apply JavaScript metaprogramming concepts by predicting descriptor behavior, using symbols and iterables, delegating with Reflect, and choosing safe proxy patterns.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Which proxy trap should validate assignments like `proxy.age = 31`?

Which proxy trap runs for this operation?
```js
"name" in proxy
```

Which proxy trap runs for this operation?
```js
delete proxy.name;
```
Which trap is used when a proxied function is called like `loggedAdd(2, 3)`?
questions.explanation: The `apply` trap intercepts calls to function proxies.

questions.prompt: Which trap is used when a proxied class is called with `new`?
questions.explanation: The `construct` trap intercepts `new ProxyConstructor(...)` and must return an object.

questions.prompt: Which choice is the best use of metaprogramming?

options.text: Using a proxy to add documented, reusable behavior that would otherwise be repeated across many objects
Using a proxy so no one can understand where values come from
Using symbol properties to store passwords securely
Using getters for expensive network requests because property reads should hide all costs

questions.explanation: Metaprogramming is best when it creates a clear reusable interface. It should not hide secrets, costly work, or surprising behavior.
